To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) non-NES students' learning is affected by their English language proficiency and by the extent to which the course content is related to their prior knowledge; and (b) the most effective pedagogy for teaching non-NES students involves a combination of: (i) explicit teaching of academic language; (ii) teaching in small groups to allow for more interaction; and (iii) teaching in English as well as in the student's native language.

(i) non-NES students are a diverse group with a wide range of abilities, needs and expectations; (ii) they need to be supported in the development of their English language skills; (iii) they need to develop a range of academic skills to be able to cope with the demands of university study; and (iv) their teachers need to be supported to help them achieve these outcomes.
